assessment.nobel_worthiness: Task-based and skill-biased accounts of labour demand, together with the China-shock evidence on trade and local labour markets, changed how economists and policymakers understand wage inequality, automation and globalisation. The work is empirically credible, widely replicated and relevant well beyond labour economics.
assessment.attribution: The Katz-Autor line on skills, tasks and wage structure and the Autor-Dorn-Hanson line on trade shocks are separable and well documented. A trio of Autor, Hanson and Katz covers both strands, and Dorn is left out because the prize allows at most three. The task framework also owes much to Acemoglu, who is not credited here and has already been recognised in 2024.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 1992 to the present. Its main findings have been replicated, debated and extended for over a decade, so the time horizon is ample.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the task and automation framework as too closely tied to Acemoglu's recently recognised work
Ongoing debate over how persistent and how large the China-shock effects were
Who among Dorn, Katz and Hanson should receive the third slot

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Melitz (2003) model of heterogeneous firms, selection and trade reshaped international trade theory and empirics, and links directly to productivity, reallocation and growth. The Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exports versus FDI extends it. Its influence on trade, macro and industrial organisation is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 Econometrica paper is the clear core. Helpman is a natural co-recipient for firm-level trade and the new-new trade theory, even though he also appears in B027. Redding is a significant contributor, but his strongest links are to later quantitative spatial and trade work. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not credited here, also contributed to the empirical foundation.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation in firm-level data and a large derivative literature. Krugman's 2008 prize covered earlier trade theory, so this builds on it rather than duplicating it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the contributions of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum
Whether the committee will want to add Redding as a third laureate
Sensitivity of welfare conclusions to the Pareto and CES functional-form assumptions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, the New Keynesian Phillips curve and the interest-rate rule framework form the working basis of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. The influence on practice and on academic macro is very large, and the topic has been recognised only indirectly in earlier prizes.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across at least eight people, which makes a three-person selection hard. Calvo and Taylor have claims on staggered pricing and wage contracts, and Taylor also on the policy rule. Woodford and Gali have claims on the modern synthesis and the NKPC. Christiano, Eichenbaum, Gertler and Smets have claims on estimated DSGE models and policy applications. Any three leave out serious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Seminal papers date from the late 1970s to the 1990s, and the framework has been used and tested for decades, including through the post-2021 inflation episode. The timing is fully mature.
uncertainties: Attribution is unusually diffuse and no trio is uncontroversial
Debate over the empirical performance of the NKPC and DSGE models after the financial crisis and the inflation surge
Whether the committee prefers a pairing centred on staggered pricing or one centred on policy rules and the full framework

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy ('Redux'), the Foundations of International Macroeconomics and the identification of the exchange-rate disconnect and related puzzles gave international macro its modern microfounded structure. The influence on academic research and on policy institutions is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pair for the 1995 Redux model and the 1996 textbook, and the puzzles paper (Obstfeld-Rogoff 2000) is jointly authored. Other contributors to open-economy macro, such as Gourinchas, Rey and Lane, are not listed. Rogoff also appears on B013, which may split support.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work dates from the early 1990s and has been confirmed by decades of use, although the empirical puzzles are still unresolved.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is viewed as mainly a framework and textbook synthesis, or as a discovery
Competition from other macro-finance and open-economy candidates
The puzzles identified are unresolved, which may be read as incomplete or as a lasting stimulus

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The inequity-aversion model of fairness (Fehr-Schmidt 1999) and the experimental evidence on reciprocity and strong reciprocity extended behavioural economics well beyond the cognitive-bias tradition. They influenced contract theory, public goods, labour and institutional design, and gave tractable models that fit experimental data.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is the leading figure across both the experiments and the theory, and Schmidt co-authored the key theory paper. Falk contributed to the field-evidence and preference-measurement side. Gächter, not credited here, was a key co-author on punishment and cooperation experiments, which complicates attribution of the experimental strand.
assessment.maturity: Core results are from the late 1990s and early 2000s, and there are two decades of replication and extension. Behavioural economics has already been recognised in 2002 and 2017, so the committee may judge this area close to saturated.
uncertainties: External validity of laboratory social-preference results
Competition from other social-preference models such as Bolton-Ockenfels and from other behavioural strands
Missing Gächter and others in the attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law-and-finance programme demonstrated empirically that legal origins and investor protection relate to financial development and corporate governance. It created a very large literature across finance, law and political economy, and shaped development policy debates.
assessment.attribution: The LLSV papers are jointly authored, with Vishny a co-author of the earlier ones. A three-person selection has to leave out one of the four credited names. Shleifer has additional claims in behavioural finance and corporate governance beyond this topic.
assessment.maturity: Foundational papers date from 1997 to 2008. The literature is mature, with extensive follow-up and critique.
uncertainties: Serious criticism of the legal-origins thesis, covering causal identification, data coding and the persistence of effects
Whether the committee will see the contribution as robust enough given the critiques
How to treat Vishny's role and the three-laureate limit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators (Arellano-Bond, Arellano-Bover, Blundell-Bond) are workhorse tools in applied microeconomics, growth, firm and labour research. Their influence on empirical practice is very broad, probably among the most used econometric methods outside regression and IV.
assessment.attribution: The estimator papers are clearly attributable to Arellano and Bond, with Blundell on the system GMM extension and Bover on the Arellano-Bover work. Bover is not credited here. Blundell and Arellano also have wider contributions to panel data and labour econometrics.
assessment.maturity: Estimators date from 1991 to 1998, and there are decades of application. Some limitations, such as instrument proliferation and weak instruments, are well understood.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to reward econometric tools whose frontier is more incremental than conceptual
Missing Bover in the attribution
Competition with other econometric candidates, including weak instruments, quantile regression and machine-learning causal inference

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrated household heterogeneity and the distribution of wealth into New Keynesian analysis, which changed how monetary and fiscal transmission are understood, particularly the role of marginal propensities to consume. They are already used in policy institutions and have strong conceptual appeal.
assessment.attribution: The Kaplan-Moll-Violante paper is joint and the three names are coherent. The approach builds on Aiyagari, Bewley, Huggett, Krusell-Smith and others, who are not credited and some of whom may have stronger claims to the underlying heterogeneous-agent framework.
assessment.maturity: The core paper is from 2018, with roughly eight years of follow-up. This is relatively young for the prize, though the research area is moving quickly.
uncertainties: Whether eight years is sufficient to judge lasting influence
Dependence on earlier heterogeneous-agent macro and the New Keynesian tradition
Competition from other macro candidates such as B025, with the stronger claim sitting in the older framework
